title: A Deadline for the Drop
premise: Sebastian Blackwood, a deniable fixer for the fictional Meridian Consulate, is haunted by a botched extraction he can't remember ordering. When a stranger named Ilse Varga repays a favor Sebastian never performed — delivering evidence of a cross-border arms deal brokered by his own agency — they become targets of an assassin codenamed Lark and pawns in a three-government cover-up. As the checkpoint shift change approaches, the only window when documents can move unseen, Sebastian must choose between loyalty to the institution that made him and the truth that could free him. In the end, Sebastian gets the dossier past the border with Ilse's help, exposes the deal at cost of his old life, and chooses exile — and love — over belonging.
about_author: Lior Kavanagh is a former diplomatic courier who spent a decade crossing borders most maps don't acknowledge. A Deadline for the Drop is their third thriller, written from a farmhouse whose location they decline to confirm.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Sebastian Blackwood, sleepless and precise, receives a package containing a favor he has no record of performing — plus a key to a Vienna locker. His POV establishes dread beneath competence; the beat is unease: someone knows his erased past.

chapters.title: Locker 44
chapters.summary: In Vienna, Sebastian opens the locker to find photographs of an arms shipment and a note signed 'I.V.' He's tailed through the Naschmarkt by a gray-eyed woman. His POV; the beat is paranoia sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: Ilse Varga
chapters.summary: The stranger, Ilse, reveals she was a courier on the shipment Sebastian supposedly extracted two years ago — the incident. She claims he saved her life and owes her the truth. Alternating POV begins; the beat is reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What the Consulate Denies
chapters.summary: Sebastian reports the contact to his handler, Marsh, who orders him to deliver Ilse for 'debriefing.' Sebastian recognizes debriefing's euphemism. His POV; the beat is first fracture between duty and conscience.

chapters.title: The Gray-Eyed Assassin
chapters.summary: Lark, the assassin, watches the pair from a rooftop and reports to an unnamed principal in three governments' shared shadow. Lark's POV introduces cold professionalism laced with private doubt; the beat is menace.

chapters.title: Run the River Route
chapters.summary: Sebastian disobeys for the first time, spiriting Ilse out of Vienna along the Danube canals. Close calls, forged papers, growing intimacy. Dual POV; the beat is adrenaline braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: Marsh's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marsh discovers Sebastian's deviation and quietly opens a file on him, revealing to readers that the 'incident' was sanctioned from above. Marsh's POV; the beat is institutional rot made personal.

chapters.title: Bratislava Safehouse
chapters.summary: Holed up with an old fixer friend, Sebastian and Ilse decode the photographs: the arms deal involves Meridian itself selling access. Ilse confesses her real motive — her brother died on that shipment. Her POV; the beat is grief becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: A tense tripartite back-channel meeting shows officials agreeing to bury the dossier and blame a dead courier: Ilse. Lark attends as security and recognizes her photo. Lark's POV; the beat is dramatic irony tightening the noose.

chapters.title: The Betrayal Option
chapters.summary: Marsh offers Sebastian full reinstatement if he delivers Ilse by dawn. Sebastian stalls, lying fluently for the first time in his career. His POV; the beat is corruption of power shown from inside its machinery.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Reconnaissance
chapters.summary: The pair scout the Berg border checkpoint and learn the shift-change window: eleven minutes when cameras hand off to human review. Ilse plans; Sebastian doubts himself. Dual POV; the beat is fragile hope.

chapters.title: Lark Closes In
chapters.summary: Lark intercepts their safehouse network, forcing a midnight flight. A brutal chase through Bratislava's underpass ends with Sebastian wounded and Lark sparing them — unexplained. Lark's POV; the beat is terror plus a crack in the assassin's certainty.

chapters.title: Why Lark Waits
chapters.summary: Lark's interlude: the principal holds leverage over Lark's family, but the dossier names the principal's own patron. Lark begins hedging. Lark's POV; the beat is the corrupt chain devouring its own links.

chapters.title: Confessions at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Wounded and cornered, Sebastian finally tells Ilse what he remembers of the incident — and admits he may have chosen to forget. Forgiveness isn't given cheaply. Dual POV; the beat is love tested against truth.

chapters.title: The Double Drop
chapters.summary: They split the dossier: bait copy for Marsh, real one moving separately. The ruse briefly works until Marsh smells it. Sebastian's POV; the beat is cunning curdling into desperation.

chapters.title: Ilse Taken
chapters.summary: Lark takes Ilse at the train station — but whispers a location and time instead of the principal's safehouse. Lark's POV; the beat is betrayal of one master in service of another debt.

chapters.title: Deals with Devils
chapters.summary: Sebastian trades his career, his records, and his silence to Marsh for Ilse's release — and secretly copies everything first. Marsh accepts, knowing. His POV; the beat is sacrifice with eyes open.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes
chapters.summary: Climax at the checkpoint during shift change: Ilse runs the documents, Sebastian draws Lark off, Marsh's men converge, and Lark turns at the last second to block them. All POVs converge; the beat is chaos resolving into choice.

chapters.title: Past the Line
chapters.summary: The dossier crosses; a journalist in The Hague receives it. Sebastian, shot again, bleeds in Ilse's car while sirens fade behind. Dual POV; the beat is exhausted, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: The story breaks: resignations in three capitals, Meridian quietly dissolved, Marsh vanishing with his ledger. Lark disappears, debt apparently settled. Multiple POVs; the beat is justice arriving imperfectly.

chapters.title: Exile Is a Country
chapters.summary: Sebastian, officially a ghost, meets Ilse where she once said her brother dreamed of living. They grieve, plan nothing, belong to each other. Dual POV; the beat is tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: A Deadline Kept
chapters.summary: Epilogue: months later, a postcard arrives from Lark — a warning that someone new is asking about the drop. Sebastian smiles, sleeps through the night for the first time, and starts packing. His POV; the beat is peace earned, vigilance kept.
